title: Three Seasons and One Short Post
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（人与自我·做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（人与自我·做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：goal　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 goal 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the coach ① set a goal that no player in the club would have described, and he said the setting was the whole of the season. The ② goal, meaning the aim itself and not the prize, ran three seasons and stayed undescribed in the book; a goal, he said, is the only thing in a club that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ goal in that club had the same short post beside it, and the ④ goal at the far end, meaning the net they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A goal, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the coach said the describing is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the goal was the whole of the matter, meaning the score and not the aim. The ⑥ goal, meaning the score and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; goal, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both an aim and a score. He said the score is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ goal had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short post. The ⑧ goal of the whole thing, the coach wrote in November, was one club and three seasons of describing; goal, he said, is either the net at the far end or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ goal I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the club. A ⑩ goal, my mother said in 1980, is the only one that improves by being described; every goal, she said, is a score that has agreed to look like an aim. She said the score was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 目标（指俱乐部里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 目标（指那个目标本身，与奖品相对）
C. 固定搭配：set a goal 设定一个目标
D. n. 球门（指留给孩子们用的那一座）
E. n. 目标（抽象总称，指一家俱乐部的目标之事）
F. n. 目标（指方案里写到、被记录过的那一个）
G. n. 进球；得分（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 进球（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: set a goal that no player in the club would have described
The goal, meaning the aim itself and not the prize
the goal at the far end

answers.why: set a goal 意为“设定一个目标”，1971 年那位教练设定了俱乐部里没有一位队员肯描述的一个目标。
goal 意为“目标”，指那个目标本身而不是奖品，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被描述。
goal 意为“目标”，指俱乐部里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一根矮矮的门柱。
goal 意为“球门”，指最远端留给孩子们用的那一座，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
goal 意为“进球、得分”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个进球就是那件事的全部。
goal 意为“进球”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个目标，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
goal 意为“目标”，指方案里写到、被记录过的那一个，到 1976 年这一个成了方案里的一行。
goal 意为“目标”，教练十一月写道，整件事的目标之事是一家俱乐部和三个赛季的描述。
goal 意为“目标”，我记得的是方案里描述过的那一个，1978 年达成了，至今仍被说成俱乐部里最安静的一个。
goal 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，一个目标是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
